I really enjoyed this game

The story was actually good, I didn't think i would be interested in Aztec history.  the cutscenes were amazing, probably my favorite part, and I thought the dialogue was enjoyable to listen to. The gameplay was fun, and after this review, I will likely play more and explore more.

The only issue I had was with the rope was disappearing around the beginning of the game. but I found online it was because my FPS was too high. Capping my FPS fixed it, so if anyone else runs into that problem, that is how you fix it.

Overall, I'd give it an 8/10. Definitely worth playing. "Eye of the Serpent"/Cenote cave is terrifying....

The game itself is well-crafted with stunning visuals, yet the overall gameplay experience leaves much to be desired. I’ve run into multiple critical problems while playing on a 240Hz monitor, listed below:
1.Certain wall panels fail to rotate into their correct orientations.
2.When being pursued by NPCs, enemies will abruptly teleport directly behind me and grab me out of nowhere. It feels like cheap jump scares, which I absolutely hate.  I tried multiple times to avoid being caught and then I realized it's just a bug caused by  my monitor.
3.Wall-climbing mechanics are extremely unresponsive: pressing the interact key “E” to latch onto adjacent walls often fails, sending me plummeting off cliffs.
4.Severe FPS drops occur randomly in certain game segments.
All of these bugs can only be mitigated by enabling half V-Sync in the graphics settings, which caps the frame rate at half my monitor’s refresh rate. It’s baffling that these high-refresh compatibility issues have never been patched since launch, even for players with high-end hardware like an RTX 4070ti. Hopefully you guys will fix it in future updates and avoid ruining this IP.

So first let me start off by saying this review is primarily about my experience playing this game on my Bazzite/ Linux machine. I quite enjoyed the gameplay, story and feel like this was an excellent conclusion to the Survivor Trilogy of games. It's unfortunate that playing through this on Linux kind of marred my overall experience in a few ways.
Now to what happened. I started this game on the free copy I had from the Epic Store, which is the Windows version running with Proton and it played perfectly for quite a while. I was running in 4K, HDR, 240hz mostly maxed out settings and the game looked fantastic. Just about the point where I reached the hidden city portion of the game, things started to go awry. I started getting crashes at certain points, broken side quests, missing NPCs, all sorts of stuff. After reading some posts online I decided to grab the game on Steam while it was on the Summer Sale and move my save over to run in the native Linux version on Steam. That worked great for quite a while and then again different crashes started popping up there too. So it became this dance of, get as far as I could in one version until I hit a blocker, move my save to the other version and progress forward, repeat. 
There was a Challenge Tomb late in the game I thought I had gotten truly stuck in both versions, until I read about some folks turning all their settings, resolution and refresh rate down to low. I followed their suggestions and was barely able to make it through that section. I did finally hit credits and overall I really enjoyed the game part of it, but I wish I had played it on my PS5 instead. I don't know for sure how many bugs I encountered were unique to my Bazzite/Linux setup or if just the overall PC version is just super buggy, but I certainly can't recommend it to anyone trying to play it on a similar setup to mine. Just wanted to share my experience for those it might be relevant to.
Realistic graphics but alot of crashes

citations.review_text:
I am shocked to see this game run on my low end laptop. Although I am running this on the lowest settings. Still I am enjoying the experience to play as a tomb raider. 
There are so many things you could do in this game. It has been 10+ hrs since I have started with the main story, I have barely completed 30% of the game. Most of the time I find myself exploring runes, challenge tombs, or some secrets. It is really fun and immersive. 
There are a lot of jungle and nature elements. Sometimes I love the scenes, sometimes it is monotonous. I wanted more action or chase sequence. Maybe in the later end of the story I'll get these. 
Also I wanted a few more outfit options and crafting freedom (only a limited things can be crafted).
Okay that's it for now. Peace out.

The Tomb Raider Survivor Trilogy really gets better with each game and not only the graphics.
I really loved the colorful jungle aesthetic of this game, it looks gorgeous and really fits the original Tomb Raider vibe in my opinion.

Highly recommended as a new approach to a cult gaming franchise.

By far the most beautiful game of the trilogie. The jungle is alive and colorful and the environment so much more interactive than in the last two games. I (personally) felt way more at home than in the icy mountain range or the dark island. Especially the tutorial was so fun well designed, that I had to get my friend to show them. The came features many underwater paths which are easy to navigate and offer good vision, not just some blurry mud water. Lara finally got some decent outfits, a personality and ACTUAL character development! The NPCs were much smarter and the story and villains felt more thought out and real than before. I didn't experience too many bugs, however the game could get laggy in environments with many NPCs. Although by far my favorite of the trilogie, it can't quite compete with its predecessor" Rise of the Tomb Raider" when it comes to its Challenge Tombs.

Shadow of the Tomb Raider brings Lara Croft’s reboot trilogy to a dark, obsessive conclusion. It stands out as the most atmospheric and exploration-heavy entry of the three—deliberately trading away non-stop firefights to double down on deep jungle survival, ancient tombs, and stealth mechanics.

If you enjoy stealth, puzzle-solving, and soaking in ancient ruins over constant gunfights, this is where the trilogy peaks.

The Core Pillars
1. Tombs, Puzzles, and Exploration First
While previous entries pushed heavy action set-pieces, Shadow shifts its focus back to what built the franchise.

Masterful Puzzle Design: The challenge tombs here are the largest, most complex, and visually stunning in the entire reboot series. They feature intricate water, fire, and gear physics that genuinely force you to pause and think.

Massive Hubs: Environments like the hidden city of Paititi act as massive, vibrant spaces filled with side quests, crypts, hidden merchant stalls, and ancient lore.

Customizable Difficulty: A fantastic feature lets you separate difficulty settings for Combat, Puzzles, and Traversal. You can turn off white paint ledges entirely, turning traversal into a true navigation challenge.

2. Terrifying Guerilla Stealth
When combat happens, Lara is no longer scrambling to survive—she is a nightmare in the brush.

Predator Mechanics: You can cover yourself in mud for camouflage, hide against vine-covered walls, and string up enemies from tree branches.

Fear Tactics: You can craft fear arrows to turn enemies against each other, making combat feel less like a standard third-person shooter and more like playing an unstoppable predator lurking in the canopy.

3. Moody Jungle Visuals
Visually, the dense South American jungle is breathtaking. Sunlight filtering through thick canopies, claustrophobic underwater caverns, and massive mud-soaked ruins create an oppressive, beautifully claustrophobic atmosphere. The underwater exploration sections—notor…

Recommended 👍

The grand finale of the reboot trilogy. It scales back on the non-stop explosions and doubles down on what the series was originally known for: actual exploration, stealth, and massive tombs.

The Good:

Peak Tomb Raiding: The tombs and puzzles in this one are the best, biggest, and most challenging of the entire trilogy. If you love exploring ancient ruins, you'll love this.

Predator Stealth: The stealth mechanics are fantastic. Coating yourself in mud to blend into walls and picking off enemies one by one from the jungle trees feels incredibly satisfying.

Insane Visuals: The South American jungles, hidden cities, and underwater sections look absolutely jaw-dropping.

The Not-So-Good:

There is way less direct combat compared to Rise and 2013, so it can feel a bit slow paced for action junkies. The pacing in the middle of the story also drags a bit.

Final Verdict:
It might not have the high-octane thrill of the first two, but it’s a beautiful and deeply satisfying conclusion that gives fans the classic "tomb raider" vibe they wanted.

8/10

just rolled credits on Shadow of the Tomb Raider after around 13 hours and ye... this was one hell of a ride.

first things first, this game is genuinely beautiful. every jungle, tomb, cave, hidden path - they all felt like something worth stopping for. and somehow it's crazy to remember this game came out back in 2018 bc it honestly doesn't feel like it. visuals have aged like fine wine. maxed out on PC, there were so many moments where I just stood there taking screenshots.

story-wise, I'd give it a solid 8/10. keeps you hooked. pacing is good. and Lara's journey wraps up trilogy in a satisfying way. my only nitpick is that Lara herself felt... colder compared to Rise of the Tomb Raider. her expressions and overall personality didn't feel as lively or emotionally expressive this time around. not bad by any means, just different.

gameplay is still super fun though. exploration is easily the best part. tombs are bigger. puzzles are actually satisfying to figure out, and I loved how much the game rewarded going off main path instead of just rushing story. stealth also got some nice upgrades. and blending into environment to take enemies out never got old.

overall? if you've somehow slept on this trilogy, definitely give it a shot. Shadow might not be my favorite Lara adventure. But it's still a gorgeous finale with great exploration, satisfying gameplay, and visuals that refuse to admit they're almost 8 years old.

I just played the story but imo its lowkey mid, has good stealth, the story was kinda dull for me, and the combat gets repetitive, i do have to say i only played the campaign and i ignored most of the side quests, id give it a 7/10

the graphics look great tho, but its definitely not worth it for full price, if interested wait for a sale, i did like it, but i dont recommend it that much

It took like 8 years to beat this game and it wasn't worth it. Somehow its a complete downgrade from both previous games. Shadow had nothing but scripted parkour segments and little actual tomb raiding or puzzles. The walls to grapple and climb blend into the environment far too much compared to TR and Rise. Both of those were much more fun to play through. Shadow was a slog to play and boring to watch. This had the most cutscenes of any of the Tomb Raider reboots and they were all boring to watch. The hidden city and game story was boring and Laura felt whinier than before. Clear to see the writing dropped in quality more than the actual gameplay.

Even though I enjoyed the previous two, I can't recommend this one. The puzzles are worse, the combat is worse, and the story is worse. Just incredibly bland. It only took 14 hours to get through the story on One with the Jungle difficulty and I would have done it faster if I didn't waste so much time collecting resources to craft upgrades I didn't need for guns I almost never used.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the raytracing option is broken and causes severe stuttering.

citations.review_text:
Shadow of the Tomb Raider is a disappointment and easily the weakest entry in the reboot trilogy for me, but I still recommend it if you want to finish Lara's story.

While I think the graphics are beautiful and Lara Croft herself remains a massive plus, the game just feels unpolished to me. The raytracing is completely broken and causes severe stuttering, so I had to disable it entirely. On top of that, I noticed cutscenes suffer from shaking cameras and out-of-sync audio, while forced camera angles ruin my immersion during gameplay.

The game balance is totally off because the world is so oversaturated with resources and XP containers, making it way too easy for me even on the highest difficulty. To make matters worse, I found the puzzles more frustrating than fun, and the final boss fight is just plain cringe. It lacks the soul and polish of its predecessors, but it is still worth playing if you want to see how her journey ends!

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as poorly optimized with severe performance issues such as broken raytracing causing stuttering, along with various visual and gameplay bugs.

citations.review_text:
Shadow of the Tomb Raider is a disappointment and easily the weakest entry in the reboot trilogy for me, but I still recommend it if you want to finish Lara's story.

While I think the graphics are beautiful and Lara Croft herself remains a massive plus, the game just feels unpolished to me. The raytracing is completely broken and causes severe stuttering, so I had to disable it entirely. On top of that, I noticed cutscenes suffer from shaking cameras and out-of-sync audio, while forced camera angles ruin my immersion during gameplay.

The game balance is totally off because the world is so oversaturated with resources and XP containers, making it way too easy for me even on the highest difficulty. To make matters worse, I found the puzzles more frustrating than fun, and the final boss fight is just plain cringe. It lacks the soul and polish of its predecessors, but it is still worth playing if you want to see how her journey ends!

I liked it, I've seen so much hate toward this one but I think it was pretty good. I've also seen some people saying this one did some things worse than Rise, and some better, I agree with that.

I liked the stealth but I think they should've polished the mechanics a lot more (maybe for the next one, I hope), covering yourself in mud and stalking and taking out groups of enemies was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome. I just wish some of the clunky stealth mechanics were better. They added so many cool things to play around with too, like the trap arrows and corpses (the corpse bombs were in Rise but I barely used them)

I liked how in the hardest difficulties (I completed it in "one with the jungle) there is no white paint in the climbable objects. This has caused me to get stuck more than a few times, sometimes REALLY hard, especially when the jump+grab were a bit buggy, which made me think I was going the wrong way more than once. But overall, it made it a lot more enjoyable than having white paint marking the obvious path. Especially figuring out puzzles. I was so close to google some of the puzzles, ended up having to do it for one, Thirsty Gods (or something like that), it didn't click at all, as well as the one with the poison and spinning tower, which I ended up brute forcing before reading the answer anyways lol.

The shooting/gunplay felt worse than Rise, somehow. I was always out of bullets, headshots were very annoying to land, most enemies have helmets, bows are all terrible. Melee was also pretty bad. So I went with stealth whenever possible, maybe that was the point?

I saw they made Score Attack more bearable compared to Rise, but I still think that mode is terrible.

The levels/maps were very cool, they looked amazing, a huge improvement over Rise, but while they were cool, they were very annoying to backtrack to get stuff you missed... especially those damn caches.

One more thing before talking about the story... Why was this the 2nd game in a row where …

This game is very beautiful and fun and Lara is hot but it's high key kind of buggy. Let me explain. 
1. When playing coop, if both players attach on the same ledge, it's likely that the other person will just fall off, which breaks the run.
2. In the Path Of Huracan, when you try to do the run on the wall, if you don't have a fixed camera angle, you won't make the jump and die. This sometimes happens in other occasions, but I noticed it happen in this tomb specifically.
3. In some Tombs when you have to make a jump, the edges are slippery or have a small rock that deny the jump and you result in a death. While this may not be a huge problem, when I played this game on highest difficulty, I had to restart the whole tomb from the beginning due to this happening. Not fun.

There are probably more things I haven't specified here and forgotten already, but most of my deaths are due to the game being buggy as hell which ruined the fun of it to some extent, but otherwise it's good.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the challenge tombs offer engaging environmental puzzles and complex layouts.

citations.review_text:
Shadow of the Tomb Raider delivers a deeply satisfying end to the trilogy, culminating in a jaw-dropping final act and a beautifully executed closing cutscene. The climax perfectly balances high-stakes cinematic chaos with Lara Croft’s emotional maturation, bringing her journey full circle from an uncertain survivor to a legendary archaeologist.

Beyond its story, the game excels everywhere it matters:

Masterclass Tomb Design: The Challenge Tombs are the largest, most atmospheric, and most rewarding environmental puzzles in the entire reboot series.
Thrilling Jungle Stealth: Striking from the canopy, slathering Lara in mud for camouflage, and terrorizing enemies with fear arrows makes combat feel like true guerrilla warfare.
Unmatched Sense of Scale: Traversing dense Peruvian rainforests, subterranean ruins, and massive underwater caverns is a visual showcase on PC.

Eidos-Montréal nails the finale, delivering an atmospheric, visually gorgeous, and narrative-rich climax that leaves a lasting impression long after the credits roll. A fitting, magnificent farewell to Lara’s origin story—highly recommended!

The ultimate finale. Unbelievably beautiful.

With 50.7 hours clocked in, Shadow is the perfect, dark conclusion to an incredible trilogy. As a huge fan, this game gave me exactly what I wanted: massive, intricate tombs, deep exploration, and brutal, terrifying stealth mechanics.

The jungle environments are jaw-droppingly gorgeous, and the optimization on PC is outstanding. It handles complex lighting and dense foliage perfectly while maintaining a rock-solid framerate. Lara’s character arc peaks here, and the atmosphere is incredibly heavy and immersive. An unforgettable experience. Highest possible recommendation!

(still like rise more)

citations.review_text: Another master class in game design for Crystal Dynamics. The graphics are amazing and the gameplay is fun and exciting, with smooth transition into cut-scenes and exciting action. The traversal of the maps stand out most impressively, with the puzzles being generally just the correct amount of challenging. Lara is a complex and vivid character and the research of the history and culture of the environment was clearly done with respect. The only gripe I have with this game is somewhat similar to the previous installment: many of the side missions can be a bit boring and tedious; however, if you adhere to the main story and save the side missions for casual future bites of the game, then it all flows pretty nicely. Highly recommend!

I'm having trouble figuring out where to start with this review. Shadow of the Tomb Raider feels like the moment when you're building a sandcastle on the beach, and no matter how much sand you try to stack on top, it keeps falling, and you know you reached the limit of how tall it can be.

It's obvious, looking at the previous two games, that the objective was to keep building on top of the foundation of the first game; they tried to stick to that formula to give players a sense of familiarity, but also some fresh mechanics each time to justify sequels. However, I think they peaked in the second game; that was the sweet spot of how much sand added to the castle, so to speak, while in this game they seemed desperate to add every single grain of sand they could fit, regardless of whether they should.

In turn, this game feels bloated; there were a lot of systems and additions that felt unnecessary and that I barely even interacted with, and my experience was mostly unaffected. It doesn't help that I feel like progression in this game was a lot less smooth than in the previous one, where it seemed a lot more thought out on how paced the unlocks were.

Another part of the game I take issue with is how the side activities were implemented; there was way too much stuff to do, and a lot of it was very unengaging, with rewards that were hit or miss. I was especially tired of the side quests; those were almost robotic in their writing, and none of them I'd go as far as saying were worth it for anything other than rewards.

The tombs and crypts ran into a different issue, though; the tombs at least felt like they had some level of quality for the most part, but there were many, and some of them were a little too similar for my taste. citations.review_text: best of the trilogy but kinda drags on during the village part

Shadow of the Tomb Raider is my least favorite game in the Survivor Trilogy, with Tomb Raider (2013) still holding the top spot. While I still think it’s a good game, it doesn’t reach the same level as the previous two entries in terms of story, pacing, or overall impact. The biggest strength of Shadow of the Tomb Raider is its gameplay. It features the most refined and polished mechanics in the trilogy, making Lara feel more capable than ever. Exploration is rewarding, combat is solid, and the tombs are easily the best in the trilogy. Even the DLC tombs are excellent, offering challenging puzzles alongside interesting side stories that add more depth to the adventure. Unfortunately, the story is the weakest in the Survivor Trilogy. While it provides a decent conclusion to Lara’s origin story, it lacks the emotional impact and memorable moments of the previous games. The pacing also suffers, particularly during the Hidden City section, where the large number of collectibles and required backtracking can become repetitive and slow the adventure down. Although the environments are visually beautiful, they often look too similar to one another. Much of the game takes place in dense jungle and ancient ruins, which can make exploration feel repetitive over time. In comparison, Rise of the Tomb Raider offered much greater environmental variety and stronger overall world design, making each new area feel more distinct and memorable. Overall, Shadow of the Tomb Raider is still a good game with the best gameplay and tomb design in the trilogy, but it’s also the weakest overall entry. Despite its excellent mechanics and impressive puzzles, its weaker story, repetitive environments, and uneven pacing prevent it from reaching the heights of Tomb Raider (2013) and Rise of the Tomb Raider. It’s still worth playing for fans of the Survivor Trilogy, especially to see Lara Croft’s origin story come to its conclusion, but it doesn’t leave the same lasting impression as its predecesso…

From the rendering to the photorealistic lighting, you’ll take a hot minute just to appreciate how this game looks. Unlike ROTTR, this game only has one weather, which is a heatwave induced summertime. An amazing adventure game set in beautiful Mesoamerican jungles.

Pros:

Atmosphere: The world in this game is absolutely amazing. Scenery, authentic spoken languages, and wildlife significantly add to the weight and immersion of the game.
Exploration and Puzzles: Combined with the great atmosphere, collecting all sorts of artifacts while running around the map feels relaxing and not tedious at all. The hidden puzzle areas are much better thought-out and harder this time around. You might get stuck in certain tombs trying to figure out how to pass through for almost an hour.
Stealth: An upgraded stealth system compared to previous games. Taking down enemies this way is much more engaging than facing them in a mindless shootout.
Lara's ass: just take a look at it 

Cons:

Story: The plot is alright, though not as interesting as those in previous games. The final boss section feels a bit disappointing, as you'd expect something tremendous after being told the bad guy is trying to acquire Kukulkan's powers.
Difficulty: I did not find the "One with the Jungle" difficulty particularly hard. Limited survival instincts don't make progression much more complicated and can easily be compensated for by buying perks early on. Resources were not as scarce as expected; I even had to upgrade guns I wasn't using just to clear out my inventory. If you want a real challenge, I'd suggest playing at maximum difficulty.
Combat: As you play, you'll find yourself breezing through enemies with ease. Aim assist on the bow, perception potions, infinite rolling, and jumping make fights feel repetitive and boring. Over the entirety of my playthrough, I only died in combat a few times.
Bugs: The first bugs appear right at the beginning of the game: glitchy ropes, Lara's hair shaking wildly, and invisible body textures. At one point, certain game elements stopped working as intended if set to high graphics settings.
